dedupe_keys.name: papers public awareness program effectiveness research survey for pipeline operators

description: PAPERS (Public Awareness Program Effectiveness Research Survey) is a biennial survey programme developed and supported by the American Petroleum Institute, the Liquid Energy Pipeline Association and INGAA, and administered by Customer Care Measurement & Consulting since 2009, so that transmission pipeline operators can meet the programme evaluation requirement of API Recommended Practice 1162. Coverage: it surveys four stakeholder audiences near US transmission pipelines (the affected public, emergency officials, public officials and excavators) on whether safety messages reach them and whether they understand the preventive, response and mitigating behaviours asked of them; it was fielded in 2007 and every two years to 2025, with operators from the largest to very small taking part. Format and access: results go to each participating company through a secure reporting portal, with company-specific results and aggregated industry benchmarks. Licence and cost: paid participation; results are proprietary and no public summaries are published. Caveats: not open data, and the sample follows the participating operators. Where access can be arranged, the awareness and stated behaviour rates could parameterise public response, excavation damage and evacuation behaviour in emergency response and hazard exposure models of pipeline corridors. It relates to the PHMSA pipeline incident data and the National Pipeline Mapping System in the catalogue.
